Jerry’s Rangers

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Meet Jerry Selwane, the unstoppable force behind Soweto's Animal Rescue and Advisory Centre (SARAC). This dynamic South African is on a mission to revolutionize animal welfare, one rescue at a time.

Unique Selling Point:
Jerry's journey began with 18 years of service at the SPCA, but he soon realized that more was needed to combat animal cruelty. So, he took a bold leap, pouring his heart (and life savings) into SARAC.

*Educating, Empowering, and Rescuing*

Jerry's vision extends far beyond rescuing animals. He's cultivating a new generation of animal advocates through:

1. "Jerry's Rangers" - empowering youth to become animal guardians.
2. Community outreach and education.
3. Collaborations with local authorities.

Summary:
Witness Jerry's unwavering dedication as he:

1. Confronts heartbreaking cases of animal abuse.
2. Navigates limited resources and funding.
3. Celebrates victories, from rehabilitated animals to successful prosecutions.

*A Legacy of Compassion*

Through Jerry's remarkable story, discover:

1. The power of one person's passion.
2. The impact of community-driven change.
3. The unwavering spirit of an animal whisperer.

*Genre:* Inspirational Short Documentary

*Target Audience:* Animal lovers, social impact enthusiasts, and anyone seeking uplifting stories.

They might be our best friends but some dog owners aren’t always worthy of their pet’s loyalty.
BREATHER
It’s a lesson Doopsie, an Alsatian cross puppy, learned the minute she was born.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC – cover entire upsound with Doopsie visuals

37:53 - because he wanted to condition doopsie to become vicious.
Doopsie's owner was her worst enemy.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC – cover entire upsound with Doopsie visuals

37:34 - … she was kept in a in a cage

38:08 - … she was so infested with ticks and flees. The skin was gone.


The troubled dog was rescued from its misery by Jerry Selwane, a man dedicating his life to the protection of domestic animals.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC – cover entire upsound with Doopsie visuals

39:51 - … if we did not rescue Doopsie at that time, she would have perished.
After six months of living hell, the rescue of a dog he called Doopsie marked the start of an enduring friendship.
BREATHER
LINK - I’m looking for the Soweto Animal Rescue and Advisory Center. I always have a fascination of people that have a love and passion for animals. I think they are really special people. But this is a first because his work mainly focuses on animals from ko kasi. And I like that!
BREATHER
Jerry has become somewhat of a legend in Soweto, where he grew up. His connection with animals makes seeing their suffering difficult to stomach.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

50:05 - … If I see an animal being ill-treated or abused and I don't assist, then I'm telling you, it's not going to be easy for me to sleep at night.
Seeing the need for animal welfare services in a community often unable to afford them, he established the Soweto Animal Rescue and Advisory Centre in 2011.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

12:09 - … we give people free service. Vaccination cllinical checks.
12:30 - Also, uh what is this, um a dipping for ticks and flees. And we also, we have some campaigns where we partner with the state veterinary. We will run some sterilization campaigns, you know, steralisation is expensive.

New VO: When we first met Jerry last year, he was one of the lone voices speaking out against dog fighting, a vicious and illegal sport still prevalent in some parts of the country.

UPS from past programme:


____ years later, word has spread about Jerry and his rehab facility and the team behind it have grown substantially.
UPSOUND – Jerry and Rangers activity group
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

11:38 I also enlisted the help of young people in Soweto. IThey are affectionately known as Jerry’s Rangers.
Jerry teaches them how to look after their pets but also tries to instill in them a sense of discipline and respect.
UPSOUND – Jerry and Rangers activity group
Sihle Nkosi joined the group a decade ago when he was just 11 - making him one of the longest serving Rangers.
SIHLE NKOSI – JERRY'S RANGER

Our job title was like clean after the pets, you see you feed them,give them water and train them also.
Like Jerry, Sihle also encourages a better way of living among the community’s younger generation.
SIHLE NKOSI – JERRY'S RANGER

We teach our young, young, teenagers to stop them from being in the streets, smoking, we see avoiding different types of deaths or other things wrong cool things.
Jerry's animal advocacy started when he worked as an inspector for the SPCA... a job he did for thirteen years.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

07:19 - ... I used all my savings, my provident fund to start this all organisation.
07:59 - … Sometimes I would go without petrol, you know. I would even hike.


At first, the facility operated from a rental property but, unable to cover costs, Jerry eventually rented out his own house and moved his family into a shack. It provided the cash he needed to keep going.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

52:35 - At one stage I would sell their PlayStation.
53:10 - And um there was uh one point where my second son, you know, he opened the fridge and he looked at the fridge and he asked me, he said, “daddy are we poor?”. Because the fridge was empty.
Jerry built kennels at the back of his shack and kept some of the rescue animals there while figuring out a more permanent solution. And it seems his dedication to animals hasn;t turned his family against him: his son, Genius, is also a Ranger.


GENIUS SELWANE – SARAC

11:58 - ... Jerry’s Rangers are Jerry’s eyes and ears. Because if they see someone abusing a dog or something like that they give Jerry a call.
13:29 - Anyone can be a Jerry's Ranger. As long as you love animals you can become a Ranger.
Jerry's hard work was eventually recognised by corporate sponsors who helped him set up the better-equipped facility SARAC now operates from.
(PAUSE on visuals of happy dogs)

New VO: As a pet-lover myself - this is me with my dogs Storm and Thore - I was keen to see the impact Jerry and his Rangers were making on these often unforgiving streets.


LINK - The sounds of joyful chaos – a testament to Jerry's tireless efforts. For him, this isn't just a shelter; it's a haven, a home.
BREATHER
The facility has offices, a clinic with an operating theater, baths, kennels, and a pet hotel.

UPS here to help segue into next theme.
Jerry learned quite early on that animal rescue work isn’t for the faint-hearted.

He was just eleven years old when he attempted his first mission: rescuing a malnourished and badly injured donkey.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

I saw these guys, and they parked their cart in front of the supermarket. - 01:22 - I think they went to buy some food or something and I unhooked that donkey hoping that that it could just run off and they beat me me so hard for that.
Dogs have a special place in Jerry’s heart. Donkeys, on the other hand, seem to have become an omen. In 2014, while returning from rescuing Doopsie, he spotted a donkey with open wounds
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

23:47 - the dog did not have fur. The fur was gone because of fleas and ticks. The guy would feed the dog whenever he felt like.
While driving home with the traumatised puppy, Jerry spotted a donkey with open wounds.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

25:35 - As I was helping that donkey. I saw three guys coming, okay? Usually when I see people coming, usually I say, “Guys, thanks for coming and assist me.” … Before I could even finish the statement, I heard someone grabbing me from behind by the throat.


The armed thugs were after his wallet. In the scuffle, Jerry was stabbed.

That was the day Jerry saved Doopsie, who is still with him today.
BREATHER
GENIUS SELWANE – JERRY'S SON

05:59 - … this man goes to a lot of dangerous places. Sometimes there are shootouts. I can’t even sleep at night until he gets home.
It’s a strange truth that some of the people clearly not able to look after their animals are the ones who put up the strongest resistance to their confiscation. Jerry, though, doesn’t back down.
UPSOUND - https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1Sp5XfAsQQ/?mibextid=qDwCgo
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

23:59 - ... when I saw that dog, I did not even want to speak to that guy because I was gonna lose it.
Jerry never takes chances with the safety of his team, especially since he often works in unfamiliar territory as far as the North West, Mpumalanga, and other provinces. Sometimes he infiltrates gangs responsible for dog fights and associated gambling. For these reasons, he works closely with law enforcement authorities.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

14:20 - Another thing is building a strong relationship with our judicial system, the magistrate courts, you know, our ministrate. So whenever I need a warrant , you know, they don't give a problem in obtaining a warrant.
14:32 - … People will cooporate because they know that if I come with a warrant then it’s going to be bad.
A man in Mpumalanga learned this the hard way. A video showing a man savagely beating a goat with a hammer trended on social media and Jerry made it his business to locate him and bring him to book. - https://www.news24.com/news24/man-appears-for-beating-goat-to-death-20141008
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

21:08 When they brought that video to my attention I could not sleep that night and I contacted some of my contacts and because after realizing that some of some authorities were trying for two years to locate and identify the perpetrator, but they could not.
Less than a day later, the man was found. The culprit offered this public apology shortly after he earned himself a criminal record for animal cruelty.
UPSOUND - https://www.facebook.com/share/v/19QfWBtHHF/?mibextid=qDwCgo
BREATHER
VO – Thankfully, the SARAC team also gets to interact with animal owners who actually want to take better care of their animals, even though they cannot always afford it. And those are the people Jerry and the Rangers, look forward to working with.
UPSOUND - Jerry driving to vaccination day location
BREATHER
LINK - Jerry and his rangers have packed their stuff and they are expected to head out to Soweto for a vaccination drive.
BREATHER
VO – It’s vaccination day in Soweto: Where every dog, big or small, receives a lifesaving shot.

Locals have brought their dogs for all-important vaccinations and Jerry and his team ensure it’s turned into something resembling a celebration.
UPSOUND – Mac and Jerry/Rangers on vaccination day
It’s a community service Jerry and the Rangers are especially proud of.
LADY PET OWNER

Explains that she's brought her child's dog to be vaccinated and expresses appreciation for SARAC's vaccination drive and how convenient and helpful it is
UPSOUND – SARAC team during vaccinations, doing physical checks on the dogs, giving advice
LINK - Seeing Jerry in action is beautiful to watch. He really loves his job and changing perceptions about animals in such communities.
BREATHER
UPSOUND – More vaccination day activity
LADY PET OWNER

speaking about how exactly the community benefits from vaccination drives such as the one today, etc
VO - Once vaccinated, each dog gets a brand new blanket and a bag of food.

Overall, it's been a productive day and over 100 dogs got their shots.
BREATHER
LINK - Brick by brick, rescue after rescue, Jerry has built a well-oiled machine that's transforming the lives of countless animals. But what's truly remarkable is that this haven didn't start here. Jerry's crusade began in the most humble of settings – his own home.
BREATHER
BREATHER
A love of animals is what brings these locals together… and it’s at least part of what binds Jerry and his family. And at the centre of it all is a dog called Doopsie - abused as a puppy, witness to an attempted Donkey rescue and now ten years old.
GENIUS SELWANE – JERRY'S SON

02:04 - I like everything about Dupsy. (laughs) Like really. The first time I saw this dog I was heartbroken. It was my first time seeing a dog like that in life.
02:23 - ... It was like family. It had a place in my heart.
JERRY SELWANE – SARAC

39:05 And she became like a wonderful soul, you know.
50:05 I know that people,when other people see, it is just an animal. For me, an animal is another living being.
